nodes.title: Kafeye danışman
nodes.description: Deniz bir cumartesiyi Elif'in iki kafesinde geçirdi; şimdi önerilerini sıralıyor

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: So, Mr Logistics Manager, you've spent a whole Saturday in my cafés. Should I be worried?
steps.translation: Evet, Bay Lojistik Müdürü, bütün bir cumartesiyi kafelerimde geçirdin. Endişelenmeli miyim?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Not worried, no. But I've written a few notes, and you won't like all of them.
steps.translation: Endişelenmene gerek yok. Ama birkaç not aldım ve hepsini sevmeyeceksin.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Go on, then. I've made you a coffee, so you have to be nice.
steps.translation: Hadi söyle bakalım. Sana kahve yaptım, yani kibar olmak zorundasın.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Fine. Let's start with the good news. The Kadıköy café is very well run. Stock is checked every evening, and almost nothing is thrown away.
steps.translation: Peki. İyi haberle başlayalım. Kadıköy'deki kafe çok iyi yönetiliyor. Stok her akşam kontrol ediliyor ve neredeyse hiçbir şey atılmıyor.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: That's because Onur has worked there for six years. He knows exactly how many croissants we sell on a rainy Tuesday.
steps.translation: Çünkü Onur orada altı yıldır çalışıyor. Yağmurlu bir salı günü kaç kruvasan sattığımızı tam olarak bilir.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Exactly, and that's the problem. Everything is in Onur's head. If he were ill for a week, nobody would know what to order.
steps.translation: Aynen, sorun da bu. Her şey Onur'un kafasında. Bir hafta hasta olsa kimse ne sipariş edeceğini bilemez.

steps.prompt: Deniz'e göre Kadıköy'deki kafenin asıl riski ne?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Hmm. He did have the flu last winter, and it was chaos. What about Moda?
steps.translation: Hmm. Geçen kış gerçekten grip olmuştu ve ortalık karışmıştı. Ya Moda?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Moda is a different story. I counted the cakes you threw away on Saturday night: fourteen. And the milk arrived at eleven, after the morning rush.
steps.translation: Moda başka bir hikâye. Cumartesi gecesi attığınız kekleri saydım: on dört. Bir de süt sabah yoğunluğundan sonra, on birde geldi.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Fourteen? I knew it was bad, but not that bad. Although, to be fair, it rained all afternoon and the terrace was empty.
steps.translation: On dört mü? Kötü olduğunu biliyordum ama bu kadar değil. Gerçi, haksızlık etmeyelim, bütün öğleden sonra yağmur yağdı ve teras boştu.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: That explains some of it, but not all. I checked your order book, and you threw away nearly as many the Saturday before, when it was sunny.
steps.translation: Bu bir kısmını açıklıyor ama hepsini değil. Sipariş defterine baktım; ondan önceki cumartesi, hava güneşliyken de neredeyse bir o kadar atmışsınız.

steps.prompt: Moda şubesinde cumartesi gecesi kaç kek atılmış?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: So here are my recommendations. First, I'd recommend that the Moda branch order cakes every day, not twice a week, at least until you know the pattern.
steps.translation: İşte önerilerim. Birincisi, Moda şubesinin en azından düzeni öğrenene kadar keki haftada iki kez değil, her gün sipariş etmesini öneririm.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: You realise you're talking like a report, don't you? 'I'd recommend that the Moda branch order.' Who talks like that?
steps.translation: Bir rapor gibi konuştuğunun farkındasın, değil mi? 'Moda şubesinin sipariş etmesini öneririm.' Kim böyle konuşur?

steps.prompt: Elif 'Who talks like that?' derken ne demek istiyor?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: People who write reports for a Dutch company all week. Anyway, second: it's essential that the milk be delivered before eight. Call the supplier and insist that they change the time, or find another one.
steps.translation: Bütün hafta bir Hollanda şirketine rapor yazan insanlar. Neyse, ikincisi: sütün saat sekizden önce teslim edilmesi şart. Tedarikçiyi ara ve saati değiştirmelerinde ısrar et, ya da başka birini bul.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Before eight? He starts his round in Kadıköy at seven, so Moda is always last.
steps.translation: Sekizden önce mi? Dağıtıma yedide Kadıköy'den başlıyor, o yüzden Moda hep sonda kalıyor.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Then ask him to reverse the route twice a week. It costs him nothing.
steps.translation: O zaman haftada iki gün güzergâhı tersine çevirmesini iste. Ona hiçbir maliyeti yok.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Maybe. But the supplier's an old friend of my father's. That'll be an awkward phone call.
steps.translation: Belki. Ama tedarikçi babamın eski bir arkadaşı. Tatsız bir telefon konuşması olacak.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: They usually are. Third, and this is the important one: I suggest that Onur write down what he knows. Not a novel, just a simple sheet: what to order, how much and when.
steps.translation: Genelde öyle olur. Üçüncüsü, en önemlisi bu: Onur'un bildiklerini yazıya dökmesini öneririm. Roman değil, basit bir sayfa: ne sipariş edilecek, ne kadar ve ne zaman.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: He'll hate that. He thinks paperwork is for people who can't remember things.
steps.translation: Bundan nefret edecek. Kâğıt işinin bir şeyleri hatırlayamayanlar için olduğunu düşünüyor.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Then don't call it paperwork. Ask him to train the Moda team instead. It's vital that someone there learn his system, and he's the only one who can teach it.
steps.translation: O zaman ona kâğıt işi deme. Onun yerine Moda ekibini eğitmesini iste. Oradan birinin onun sistemini öğrenmesi hayati önemde ve bunu öğretebilecek tek kişi o.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: That's actually clever. He loves being the expert.
steps.translation: Bu aslında zekice. Uzman olmaya bayılır.

steps.prompt: Elif, Deniz'in Onur'la ilgili son önerisine nasıl yaklaşıyor?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I know. I've met him. One last thing: I'd suggest that you not open a third café this year.
steps.translation: Biliyorum. Onunla tanıştım. Son bir şey: bu yıl üçüncü bir kafe açmamanı öneririm.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Who said anything about a third café?
steps.translation: Üçüncü kafeden kim bahsetti?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Onur did. Apparently you've been looking at places in Üsküdar.
steps.translation: Onur. Anlaşılan Üsküdar'da yer bakıyormuşsun.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Onur talks too much. Fine, I'll think about it. So, what do I owe you for all this?
steps.translation: Onur çok konuşuyor. Tamam, düşüneceğim. Peki, bütün bunlar için sana ne borçluyum?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Another coffee. And one of those fourteen cakes, before it ends up in the bin.
steps.translation: Bir kahve daha. Bir de o on dört kekten biri, çöpe gitmeden önce.

steps.prompt: Deniz'in son cümlesindeki 'those fourteen cakes' neyi kastediyor?

nodes.title: Okuma: Kurum raporu
nodes.description: Bir iç değerlendirme raporunda amaç, yöntem, bulgular ve sonuç

exercises.passage:
Clarke & Vos, Istanbul Office
Internal Review: Why New Employees Leave in Their First Year
Prepared for: Deniz, Head of the Istanbul office
Prepared by: Selma Korkmaz, People and Culture

1. Purpose
This review was commissioned after an unusually high number of new employees left the Istanbul office within twelve months of joining. Its purpose is to establish why this is happening and where the office could act most effectively. Recommendations will be presented separately, once the findings have been discussed with team leaders.

2. Background
Between January and December of last year, the office hired forty-two people, most of them for the warehouse coordination and customer operations teams. Fifteen of them had left by the end of the year, eleven within their first three months. Replacing an employee is not cheap. Our own estimate, which includes recruitment fees, overtime for colleagues covering the vacancy and the time spent on training, puts the cost at roughly four months' salary per person. Harder to measure, but arguably just as damaging, is the effect on the teams left behind, who repeatedly invest time in colleagues who then disappear.

3. Method
The review drew on three sources. First, we held exit interviews with twelve of the fifteen people who left; the remaining three declined to take part. Second, thirty current employees who joined during the year completed an anonymous questionnaire. Third, we spoke to all six team leaders individually. We should stress that the numbers involved are small, and the findings should be read as indications rather than proof.

4. Findings
4.1 The first week
The most consistent complaint concerned the first week. Several leavers described arriving to find that no desk, laptop or system access had been prepared. One said that she had spent her first two days "reading the company website because there was nothing else to do". Among current employees, fewer than half said that their first week had been well organised.

4.2 Unclear expectations
Many new staff reported that they did not know how their performance would be judged. Job descriptions had often been written for recruitment purposes and bore little resemblance to the work itself. Team leaders, for their part, admitted that they rarely set goals for new starters in writing, assuming that expectations would "become obvious".

4.3 Isolation
New employees in the customer operations team work shifts, and several said that they had met their own team leader only two or three times in their first month. Those who had been informally paired with an experienced colleague were noticeably more positive about their experience. Of the twelve leavers interviewed, only one had had such a colleague.

4.4 Pay and workload
Somewhat surprisingly, pay was mentioned by only four leavers, and in each case as a secondary reason. Workload was raised more often, particularly in the warehouse coordination team during the peak season in November and December.

5. Conclusions
The evidence suggests that the office does not have a recruitment problem so much as an arrival problem. People appear to decide very early whether they will stay, and the first weeks are when that decision is made. None of the issues identified requires significant investment; most could be addressed through better planning and clearer responsibilities. The team leaders we spoke to were open to change, although two of them asked that any new procedures not add to their own workload during busy periods.

Recommendations will be presented at the management meeting on 14 March.
exercises.question: Raporun vardığı ana sonuç ne?
options: Salaries are too low to keep new staff.
The office should hire fewer people.
New staff leave mainly because of their first weeks.
Team leaders refuse to change anything.

Second, thirty current employees who joined during the year completed an anonymous questionnaire. Third, we spoke to all six team leaders individually. 4.1 The first week
The most consistent complaint concerned the first week. Several leavers described arriving to find that no desk, laptop or system access had been prepared. One said that she had spent her first two days "reading the company website because there was nothing else to do". Among current employees, fewer than half said that their first week had been well organised.

4.2 Unclear expectations
Many new staff reported that they did not know how their performance would be judged. Job descriptions had often been written for recruitment purposes and bore little resemblance to the work itself. Team leaders, for their part, admitted that they rarely set goals for new starters in writing, assuming that expectations would "become obvious".

4.3 Isolation
New employees in the customer operations team work shifts, and several said that they had met their own team leader only two or three times in their first month. Those who had been informally paired with an experienced colleague were noticeably more positive about their experience. Of the twelve leavers interviewed, only one had had such a colleague.

4.4 Pay and workload
Somewhat surprisingly, pay was mentioned by only four leavers, and in each case as a secondary reason. Workload was raised more often, particularly in the warehouse coordination team during the peak season in November and December.

The evidence suggests that the office does not have a recruitment problem so much as an arrival problem. People appear to decide very early whether they will stay, and the first weeks are when that decision is made. None of the issues identified requires significant investment; most could be addressed through better planning and clearer responsibilities. exercises.prompt: Okuduğun Clarke & Vos raporu için 220–260 kelimelik "6. Recommendations" bölümünü yaz. Kısa bir girişle bulgulara gönderme yap; en az üç bulguya alt başlıklarla (6.1, 6.2…) birer öneri getir; ekip liderlerinin kaygısına cevap ver ve ilerlemenin nasıl ölçüleceğini belirt. Resmî öneri kalıplarını (recommend that…, it is essential that…) subjunctive ile kullan.
exercises.model:
6. Recommendations

In light of the findings above, we propose the following measures. None of them requires significant investment, and all of them could be introduced before the next hiring round in May.

6.1 Preparing the first week
We recommend that a named person in each team be responsible for the arrival of every new starter. It is essential that the desk, laptop and system access be ready before the employee's first day, and that a written plan for the first week be sent to them in advance.

6.2 Setting clear expectations
It is important that each new employee receive written goals for their first three months. We suggest that team leaders agree these goals with the new starter during the first week and review them at the end of each month.

6.3 Reducing isolation
We strongly recommend that every new employee be paired with an experienced colleague from the same team for at least the first two months. In the customer operations team, it is vital that the pair work at least some of the same shifts.

6.4 Protecting team leaders
Given the concerns raised by team leaders, we propose that the onboarding tasks in 6.1 not be added to their workload during the peak season. Instead, the People and Culture team should coordinate the process.

6.5 Measuring progress
Finally, we recommend that the office repeat this review in twelve months, so that the effect of these changes can be assessed. If first-year departures have not fallen by then, the question of workload should be examined in more detail.

units.title: Ben de öyle
units.description: Eksiltme ve yerine koyma (so do I, neither have I, I hope so, if so, if not) ile kısa ve doğal tepkiler ver
units.guide:
## Yapı
İngilizce, aynı fiili ya da cümleyi tekrar etmemek için **eksiltme** (ellipsis) ve **yerine koyma** (substitution) kullanır. Türkçedeki "Ben de", "Umarım öyle", "Değilse" gibi kısa cevapların İngilizcesi şöyle kurulur:

| Türkçe | İngilizce | Kural |
|---|---|---|
| Ben de (olumlu) | So do I. / So have I. / So am I. | so + yardımcı fiil + özne |
| Ben de (olumsuz) | Neither do I. / Nor have I. | neither/nor + yardımcı fiil + özne |
| Umarım öyledir / değildir | I hope so. / I hope not. | so ve not bütün cümlenin yerini tutar |
| Sanırım / Sanmıyorum | I think so. / I don't think so. | think, suppose, expect, be afraid ile |
| Öyleyse / Değilse | if so / if not | koşul cümlesini kısaltır |
| Yapmalıydım / Gelmek isterdim | I should have. / I'd love to. | yardımcı fiilde ya da to'da dur |

Yardımcı fiil önceki cümleye göre seçilir: *Kerem drinks his tea black.* → *So does Sam.* / *I've never been there.* → *Neither have I.* Günlük konuşmada **Me too** ve **Me neither** de doğaldır ama resmî yazıda **So do I / Neither do I** tercih edilir.

## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Hızlı ve doğal bir arkadaş sohbetinde kısaltılmış cevapları (so have I, if not, I hope not) duyunca anlayabilirsin.
- Bir fikre ya da habere kısa, doğal ve uygun tepkiler verebilirsin (Fair enough, Same here, Tell me about it).
- Aynı fiili tekrar etmeden katılabilir, katılmayabilir ve tahmin bildirebilirsin.
- Bir hafta sonu planını ya da küçük bir aksiliği 90 saniyede, akıcı bir şekilde anlatabilirsin.

## Strateji
- Dinlerken kısa cevabın neyin yerini tuttuğunu bul: *So have I* duyduğunda önceki cümledeki present perfect fiili hatırla.
- Hızlı konuşmada yardımcı fiiller zayıflar: *so's Deniz*, *I'd love to*, *if not*. Vurgu genellikle özneye düşer: *So do I*.
- Gölgeleme yaparken kısa tepkilerin tonunu da taklit et: *Tell me about it!* yakınma, *Fair enough* kabul bildirir.
- Konuşurken bütün cümleyi tekrarlamak yerine yardımcı fiilde dur: *I didn't want to, but I did.*
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle; sonra metni açıp eksiltilen kısımları kendin tamamla.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ I hope it. / I hope yes. ✅ I hope **so**. (Türkçedeki "Umarım öyle" İngilizcede **so** ile kurulur; olumsuzu **I hope not**.)
- ❌ Neither I am. / Me too not. ✅ **Neither am I.** / **Me neither.** (neither'dan sonra yardımcı fiil özneden önce gelir.)

steps.translation: Sen bir harikasın. Saat üçten beri bunun hayalini kuruyorum.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: So have I. My whole afternoon was one video call after another.
steps.translation: Ben de. Bütün öğleden sonram arka arkaya görüntülü görüşmelerle geçti.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Rotterdam again?
steps.translation: Yine mi Rotterdam?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Rotterdam, then Antwerp, then Rotterdam again. And guess what? My boss is coming over next week.
steps.translation: Rotterdam, sonra Anvers, sonra yine Rotterdam. Bil bakalım ne oldu? Patronum gelecek hafta geliyor.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Coming here? To Istanbul?
steps.translation: Buraya mı? İstanbul'a mı?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Apparently so. Four days. She wants to see our warehouse in Ümraniye and, I quote, 'the real city'.
steps.translation: Öyle görünüyor. Dört gün. Ümraniye'deki depomuzu ve aynen aktarıyorum, 'gerçek şehri' görmek istiyor.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Well, if she wants the real city, bring her here. I'll make her a proper breakfast.
steps.translation: Gerçek şehri istiyorsa buraya getir. Ona adam gibi bir kahvaltı hazırlarım.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I was hoping you'd say that. Would Saturday work?
steps.translation: Bunu söylemeni umuyordum. Cumartesi olur mu?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: I think so. If not, Sunday's quieter anyway. Moda gets a bit crazy on Saturdays.
steps.translation: Sanırım olur. Olmazsa pazar zaten daha sakin. Moda cumartesileri biraz çılgına dönüyor.

steps.prompt: Deniz'in patronu İstanbul'da kaç gün kalacak?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Is she the one who sent you that very long email about the coffee machine?
steps.translation: Sana kahve makinesiyle ilgili o upuzun e-postayı gönderen o mu?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: The very same. But to be fair, she's lovely in person. She just writes like a lawyer.
steps.translation: Ta kendisi. Ama hakkını vermek lazım, yüz yüze çok tatlı biri. Sadece avukat gibi yazıyor.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Ha, so does my mother.
steps.translation: Ha, benim annem de öyle.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Speaking of emails, Sam, did you hear back from the teacher-training people?
steps.translation: E-posta demişken, Sam, öğretmen eğitimi ekibinden cevap geldi mi?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: I did, this morning. They want me to run the whole spring programme. Twelve teachers, eight weeks.
steps.translation: Geldi, bu sabah. Bütün bahar programını benim yürütmemi istiyorlar. On iki öğretmen, sekiz hafta.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Sam! That's brilliant. You wanted that, didn't you?
steps.translation: Sam! Harika. Bunu istiyordun, değil mi?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: I did. I still do, I think. It's just that I'd have to give up two of my evening classes.
steps.translation: İstiyordum. Sanırım hâlâ istiyorum. Sadece akşam derslerimden ikisini bırakmam gerekecek.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: And you don't want to.
steps.translation: Sen de bırakmak istemiyorsun.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Not really, no. Some of those students have been with me for three years. It feels a bit like abandoning them.
steps.translation: Pek istemiyorum, hayır. O öğrencilerin bazıları üç yıldır benimle. Onları yüzüstü bırakıyormuşum gibi geliyor.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Could they join one of your other groups?
steps.translation: Diğer gruplarından birine katılamazlar mı?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Some could, I suppose. Not all of them, though. The Thursday lot can only come on Thursdays.
steps.translation: Bazıları katılabilir sanırım. Ama hepsi değil. Perşembe grubu sadece perşembeleri gelebiliyor.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Then ask the programme to move one session. If they really want you, they'll say yes.
steps.translation: O zaman programdan bir oturumu kaydırmalarını iste. Seni gerçekten istiyorlarsa evet derler.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: You make it sound easy.
steps.translation: Kolaymış gibi anlatıyorsun.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: It usually is. People rarely ask, that's the problem. I learned that the hard way at work.
steps.translation: Genelde kolaydır. İnsanlar nadiren sorar, sorun bu. Ben bunu işte zor yoldan öğrendim.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: He's right, you know. I never asked my landlord for anything for five years. Then I did, and he said yes straight away.
steps.translation: Haklı, biliyor musun. Beş yıl boyunca ev sahibimden hiçbir şey istemedim. Sonra istedim ve hemen evet dedi.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Fine. I'll write to them tonight. Well, tomorrow morning. If I write tonight, I'll only say something silly.
steps.translation: Tamam. Bu akşam onlara yazacağım. Yani yarın sabah. Bu akşam yazarsam saçma bir şey söylerim.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Very wise.
steps.translation: Çok akıllıca.

steps.prompt: Sam e-postayı ne zaman yazmaya karar veriyor?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: By the way, has either of you got plans for the twentieth? Kerem's band is playing in Karaköy.
steps.translation: Bu arada, ikinizin ayın yirmisinde bir planı var mı? Kerem'in grubu Karaköy'de çalıyor.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Kerem has a band? Since when?
steps.translation: Kerem'in grubu mu var? Ne zamandan beri?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Since about March, apparently. He plays bass. Badly, according to him, but I don't believe him.
steps.translation: Mart'tan beri galiba. Bas çalıyor. Kendisine göre kötü çalıyor ama ona inanmıyorum.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I'm in. I've been looking for an excuse to leave the office before eight.
steps.translation: Ben varım. Ofisten sekizden önce çıkmak için bir bahane arıyordum.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: So have I. Well, not the office. The marking.
steps.translation: Ben de. Yani ofis değil. Kâğıt okuma.

steps.prompt: Sam 'So have I' derken neyi kastediyor?
choices: O da grubu daha önce izledi

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Great. I'll get three tickets, then. If they've sold out, we'll just stand outside and cheer.
steps.translation: Harika. O zaman üç bilet alırım. Tükendiyse dışarıda durup alkışlarız.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Knowing Kerem's fan base, they won't have sold out.
steps.translation: Kerem'in hayran kitlesini bildiğim için, biletlerin tükenmiş olacağını sanmam.

steps.prompt: Deniz biletler hakkında ne ima ediyor?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Deniz! Be nice.
steps.translation: Deniz! Kibar ol.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I am being nice. I'm being realistic. There's a difference.
steps.translation: Kibarım zaten. Gerçekçiyim. Arada fark var.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Is there? I'm not sure there is, with you.
steps.translation: Var mı? Senin söz konusu olduğunda var mı, emin değilim.

steps.prompt: Arkadaşlar arasındaki konuşmanın tonu nasıl?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Right, more tea? The rain's not stopping any time soon.
steps.translation: Peki, bir çay daha? Yağmur yakında dinecek gibi değil.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: I hope not. I'm not going anywhere.
steps.translation: Umarım dinmez. Hiçbir yere gitmiyorum.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Neither am I. Pour away.
steps.translation: Ben de gitmiyorum. Doldur bakalım.

units.title: Bununla birlikte
units.description: İleri bağlaçlar (whereas, notwithstanding, given that, insofar as) ile iki şeyi karşılaştır
units.guide:
## Yapı
C1 düzeyinde karşılaştırma ve karşıtlık yalnızca *but* ve *however* ile kurulmaz. Bu bağlaçlar fikirler arasındaki ilişkiyi daha kesin gösterir:

| Bağlaç | Anlamı | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| whereas / while | oysa, -ken (iki şeyi karşılaştırır) | I read on paper, **whereas** my sister listens. |
| given that | -dığı düşünülürse, -dığına göre | **Given that** the library closes at six, let's start early. |
| insofar as | -dığı ölçüde, -dığı kadarıyla | The plan is fair **insofar as** everyone pays the same. |
| in that | -mesi bakımından, -dığı için | The library is ideal **in that** it is quiet. |
| notwithstanding | -e rağmen (resmî) | **Notwithstanding** the rain, the event went ahead. |
| albeit | -se de (sıfat ya da isimden önce) | It was useful, **albeit** a little long. |
| that said / even so | bununla birlikte, yine de | **That said**, no format does the work for you. |

*whereas* ve *given that* arkasından tam cümle alır; *notwithstanding* ise bir isim öbeği alır, tıpkı *despite* gibi. *Insofar as* bir iddiayı sınırlar: "yalnızca şu açıdan doğru".

## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- İki seçeneği karşılaştıran uzun bir makalede yazarın tutumunu ve metnin düzenini anlayabilirsin.
- Bir radyo programında farklı görüşleri ve konuşmacıların örtük mesajlarını ayırt edebilirsin.
- whereas, given that, insofar as ve notwithstanding ile fikirler arasındaki ilişkiyi kesin bir şekilde kurabilirsin.
- 230–290 kelimelik, giriş, karşılaştırma ve sonuç bölümleri olan bir karşılaştırma denemesi yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- Okurken her paragrafın işlevini kenara not et: benzerlik mi, fark mı, örnek mi, sonuç mu?
- Bağlaçlar yol işaretidir: *whereas* bir karşıtlık, *given that* bir gerekçe, *notwithstanding* bir itiraf ve ardından gelen asıl fikir demektir.
- Yazarın tutumunu sıfat ve zarflardan yakala: *unfortunately*, *beautifully*, *simply the wrong question*.
- Yazarken iki şeyi ayrı paragraflarda anlat, sonra ortak noktayı ve kendi sonucunu ver. Aynı bağlacı iki kez kullanma.

## Model metin
> Library or Home? Two Ways to Study
>
> Most students eventually have to decide where they do their best work. For many, the choice is between the public library and their own desk at home. Both have clear advantages, but they suit different tasks and different personalities.
>
> The library's greatest strength is its atmosphere. When you are surrounded by people who are working, it is hard to drift towards the sofa or the fridge. Given that most of us are easily distracted, this quiet pressure can be surprisingly effective. A library also offers resources that few homes have, from reference books to reliable Wi-Fi and, in many cases, free printing.
>
> Studying at home, by contrast, offers comfort and freedom. You can make tea whenever you like, read aloud and start at six in the morning if that is when your mind is sharpest. Whereas the library sets your timetable, home lets you set your own. The problem is that the same freedom makes it very easy to waste an afternoon.
>
> Notwithstanding their differences, the two places have one thing in common: neither works without a plan. A student who arrives at the library with no clear goal will waste time just as easily as one who stays at home.
>
> In my view, the best solution is to use both. The library is ideal for long, demanding tasks such as revising for an exam, insofar as it removes temptation. Home is better for short tasks and for creative work that benefits from a relaxed mood. Choosing the right place for the right task matters far more than choosing one place for ever.

Yapı: başlık, konuyu ve iki seçeneği tanıtan giriş, her seçenek için bir paragraf, ortak nokta ve kişisel sonuç. Bağlaçlar her paragrafta farklı bir ilişki kuruyor: **Given that** gerekçe, **Whereas** karşıtlık, **Notwithstanding** itiraf, **insofar as** sınırlama.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ Notwithstanding the library is small, it is popular. ✅ **Although** the library is small, it is popular. / **Notwithstanding its size**, it is popular. (notwithstanding'den sonra cümle değil, isim öbeği gelir.)
- ❌ Library is ideal for long tasks. ✅ **The** library is ideal for long tasks. (Belirli ya da genel kurum olarak kütüphaneden söz ederken **the** gerekir: the library, the cinema.)

nodes.title: Sessiz kat, konuşan kat
nodes.description: Bir radyo programında kütüphane müdürü ve bir dinleyici değişikliği tartışıyor

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: Good evening and welcome to Shelf Life. I'm Nadia Haddad. My guest tonight runs a library that has, let's say, divided opinion. Aoife Brennan, welcome.
steps.translation: İyi akşamlar, Shelf Life'a hoş geldiniz. Ben Nadia Haddad. Bu akşamki konuğum, diyelim ki görüşleri ikiye bölen bir kütüphanenin müdürü. Aoife Brennan, hoş geldiniz.

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: Thanks, Nadia. Divided is a polite word for it, but I'll take it.
steps.translation: Teşekkürler Nadia. 'Bölmek' bunun kibar bir ifadesi ama kabul ediyorum.

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: So, for listeners who haven't been, what did you actually change?
steps.translation: Peki, oraya hiç gitmemiş dinleyiciler için soralım: Tam olarak neyi değiştirdiniz?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: We split the building in two. The ground floor is now what we call the talking floor, whereas the top floor is completely silent. No phones, no whispering, nothing.
steps.translation: Binayı ikiye böldük. Zemin kat artık 'konuşan kat' dediğimiz yer, oysa üst kat tamamen sessiz. Telefon yok, fısıltı yok, hiçbir şey yok.

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: And before that?
steps.translation: Peki öncesinde?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: Before that, the whole building was officially quiet, and in practice it was neither quiet nor lively. People whispered, phones buzzed, and everyone was annoyed with everyone else.
steps.translation: Öncesinde bütün bina resmî olarak sessizdi ama pratikte ne sessizdi ne de canlı. İnsanlar fısıldaşıyor, telefonlar titriyor, herkes herkese kızıyordu.

steps.prompt: Değişiklikten önce kütüphanede durum nasıldı?
choices: Ne gerçekten sessizdi ne de canlı
steps.answer: Ne gerçekten sessizdi ne de canlı

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: And whose idea was the split?
steps.translation: Peki bölme fikri kimindi?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: Honestly? A fourteen-year-old's. She wrote in our suggestions box that the library felt like a waiting room for something that never happened.
steps.translation: Dürüst olayım mı? On dört yaşında bir kızın. Öneri kutumuza kütüphanenin hiç gerçekleşmeyen bir şeyin bekleme salonu gibi hissettirdiğini yazmıştı.

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: Why not just enforce the silence more strictly?
steps.translation: Neden sessizlik kuralını daha sıkı uygulamadınız?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: We tried. Given that we have two staff members on most evenings, it simply wasn't realistic. You can't police two floors with two people.
steps.translation: Denedik. Çoğu akşam iki görevlimiz olduğu düşünülürse bu hiç gerçekçi değildi. İki kişiyle iki katı denetleyemezsiniz.

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: Fair enough. So what happens on the talking floor?
steps.translation: Anlaşılır. Peki konuşan katta neler oluyor?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: Homework clubs, a chess corner, conversation groups for people learning Turkish or English, and on Thursdays, a knitting circle that is, frankly, the loudest group in the building.
steps.translation: Ödev kulüpleri, bir satranç köşesi, Türkçe ya da İngilizce öğrenenler için sohbet grupları ve perşembeleri, açıkçası binanın en gürültülü grubu olan bir örgü grubu.

steps.prompt: Konuşan katta perşembe günleri hangi grup toplanıyor?

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: Now, we had a lot of messages about this. Piotr is on the line. Piotr, you're not a fan, I gather?
steps.translation: Bu konuda çok mesaj aldık. Hatta Piotr var. Piotr, anladığım kadarıyla pek hayranı değilsiniz?

steps.speaker: Piotr
steps.text: Not really, no. I've used that library for twenty years. It used to be the one place in the neighbourhood where nobody expected anything from you.
steps.translation: Pek değilim, hayır. Yirmi yıldır o kütüphaneyi kullanıyorum. Mahallede kimsenin sizden hiçbir şey beklemediği tek yerdi.

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: And the top floor still is, Piotr. That was the whole point.
steps.translation: Üst kat hâlâ öyle, Piotr. Bütün mesele de buydu.

steps.speaker: Piotr
steps.text: Insofar as it's quiet, yes. But it's smaller, and by four o'clock every seat is taken. Notwithstanding all the good intentions, I lost my favourite table.
steps.translation: Sessiz olduğu ölçüde, evet. Ama daha küçük ve saat dörtte her yer dolu oluyor. Bütün iyi niyete rağmen en sevdiğim masayı kaybettim.

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: That sounds like a fairly personal complaint.
steps.translation: Bu oldukça kişisel bir şikâyet gibi geliyor.

steps.speaker: Piotr
steps.text: It is personal! I wrote half a novel at that table.
steps.translation: Kişisel tabii! O masada yarım roman yazdım.

steps.prompt: Piotr'un değişikliğe karşı tutumu nasıl?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: Then you must come and see me. We're adding twenty desks upstairs in the spring, and I'll personally make sure one of them is by a window.
steps.translation: O zaman gelip beni görmelisiniz. Baharda üst kata yirmi masa ekliyoruz ve birinin pencere kenarında olmasını bizzat sağlayacağım.

steps.speaker: Piotr
steps.text: Well, if that happens, I might forgive you.
steps.translation: Öyle olursa sizi affedebilirim.

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: Aoife, the figures. Has it worked?
steps.translation: Aoife, rakamlara gelelim. İşe yaradı mı?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: Visits are up by about a third, according to our own counts, and loans have risen too, albeit more slowly. What surprised me is who's coming. We see far more teenagers than before.
steps.translation: Kendi sayımlarımıza göre ziyaretler yaklaşık üçte bir arttı, ödünç almalar da arttı ama daha yavaş. Beni şaşırtan, gelenlerin kim olduğu. Eskisinden çok daha fazla genç görüyoruz.

steps.prompt: Aoife'nin ödünç almalarla ilgili sözünden ne çıkarılabilir?
choices: Yeni gelenlerin hepsi kitap ödünç almıyor
steps.answer: Yeni gelenlerin hepsi kitap ödünç almıyor

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: Why do you think that is?
steps.translation: Sizce bunun nedeni ne?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: Teenagers need somewhere to be together that isn't a café, because cafés cost money. A library that lets them talk is a library they'll actually use.
steps.translation: Gençlerin bir arada olabilecekleri, kafe olmayan bir yere ihtiyacı var, çünkü kafeler para ister. Konuşmalarına izin veren bir kütüphane, gerçekten kullanacakları bir kütüphanedir.

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: And the critics who say a library should be quiet, full stop?
steps.translation: Peki kütüphane sessiz olmalı, nokta, diyen eleştirmenler?

steps.speaker: Aoife
steps.text: I understand them. I'm one of them, in a way. That's precisely why we protected the top floor. A library can be a refuge and a meeting place, as long as you're honest about which room is which.
steps.translation: Onları anlıyorum. Bir bakıma ben de onlardanım. Üst katı tam da bu yüzden koruduk. Hangi odanın ne işe yaradığı konusunda dürüst olduğunuz sürece bir kütüphane hem sığınak hem de buluşma yeri olabilir.

steps.prompt: Aoife'ye göre kütüphanenin iki işlevi nasıl bir arada var olabilir?
choices: Her işleve ayrı bir alan ayrılarak
steps.answer: Her işleve ayrı bir alan ayrılarak

steps.speaker: Nadia
steps.text: Aoife Brennan, thank you. And Piotr, I hope you get your window.
steps.translation: Aoife Brennan, teşekkürler. Piotr, umarım pencerenize kavuşursunuz.

steps.speaker: Piotr
steps.text: So do I, Nadia. So do I.
steps.translation: Ben de umarım, Nadia. Ben de umarım.

exercises.passage:
Ears or Eyes? Audiobooks and Print Compared

Ten years ago, admitting that you had "read" a novel by listening to it might have raised an eyebrow at a dinner party. Today, audiobooks are one of the fastest-growing parts of publishing, and an old question has returned in a new form: is listening to a book really the same as reading it? The honest answer, as so often, is that it depends on what you want from the book.

Start with what the two formats share. Whether a story reaches us through the eyes or the ears, the brain seems to do much of the same work once the words have arrived. Several small studies suggest that, for simple narrative, people who listen and people who read tend to remember the plot about equally well. Insofar as a novel is a story to be followed, then, the format may matter less than purists like to think.

The differences appear when the text becomes harder. Print lets the reader control the pace: you can slow down, read a difficult sentence again or glance back at a chart. A listener, by contrast, is carried along at the speed of the narrator. Rewinding is possible, of course, but few people do it, and even fewer do it at the right moment. Given that dense non-fiction relies on exactly this kind of pausing and checking, many teachers still recommend paper, or at least a screen, for anything that has to be studied rather than simply enjoyed.

Attention is the other key factor. Reading a page is rarely something we do while cooking or driving, whereas listening almost always is. This is both the great strength of audiobooks and their weakness. They turn a long commute into an hour with Dickens, yet they also invite the mind to wander. Most listeners will know the moment when they suddenly realise that three minutes have passed and they have no idea what the narrator has just said.

Notwithstanding these limits, audio has advantages that print cannot easily match. A skilled narrator brings out humour, irony and accents that a silent reader might miss. Poetry and drama were written to be heard in the first place, and many people say they understood Shakespeare only when they heard the lines spoken aloud. For readers with dyslexia or poor eyesight, meanwhile, audiobooks are not a second-best option but the door to books in general.

Cost and habit complicate the picture further. In some countries, a subscription gives access to thousands of titles for the price of two or three printed books, while public libraries increasingly lend audio files free of charge. On the other hand, a printed book can be borrowed, annotated, passed on and kept for decades, and it never needs charging.

So which is better? The question may simply be the wrong one. A more useful approach is to match the format to the purpose. Light fiction on a long walk works beautifully in the ears; a history book you want to argue with probably belongs on paper, pen in hand. Some readers now combine the two, listening to a chapter on the bus and then reading the next one at home. That said, no format can do the reader's work for them. Whether the words arrive by eye or by ear, what turns them into understanding is attention, and that, unfortunately, cannot be downloaded.
exercises.question: Metnin ana fikri nedir?
options: Audiobooks are slowly replacing printed books
Print is always the better choice for serious readers
The best format depends on the purpose of the reading
Listening to a book is a form of cheating
exercises.explanation: "The best format depends on the purpose of the reading" doğru: yazar girişte "it depends on what you want from the book" diyor ve sonuçta "match the format to the purpose" öneriyor.

Başlık, giriş, her seçenek için bir paragraf, ortak nokta ve kendi sonucun olsun. En az dört farklı ileri bağlaç kullan (whereas, given that, insofar as, notwithstanding, by contrast…).
exercises.model:
Library or Home? Two Ways to Study

Most students eventually have to decide where they do their best work. For many, the choice is between the public library and their own desk at home. Both have clear advantages, but they suit different tasks and different personalities.

The library's greatest strength is its atmosphere. When you are surrounded by people who are working, it is hard to drift towards the sofa or the fridge. Given that most of us are easily distracted, this quiet pressure can be surprisingly effective. A library also offers resources that few homes have, from reference books to reliable Wi-Fi and, in many cases, free printing.

Studying at home, by contrast, offers comfort and freedom. You can make tea whenever you like, read aloud and start at six in the morning if that is when your mind is sharpest. Whereas the library sets your timetable, home lets you set your own. The problem is that the same freedom makes it very easy to waste an afternoon.

Notwithstanding their differences, the two places have one thing in common: neither works without a plan. A student who arrives at the library with no clear goal will waste time just as easily as one who stays at home.

In my view, the best solution is to use both. The library is ideal for long, demanding tasks such as revising for an exam, insofar as it removes temptation. Home is better for short tasks and for creative work that benefits from a relaxed mood. Choosing the right place for the right task matters far more than choosing one place for ever.
checklist: Başlık ve iki seçeneği tanıtan bir giriş yazdın
Her seçeneği ayrı bir paragrafta, en az bir örnekle anlattın
En az dört farklı ileri bağlaç kullandın (whereas, given that, insofar as, notwithstanding…)

units.title: Ortaya çıkmak
units.description: İleri phrasal verb'ler (come across as, bring about, play down, turn out) ile bir deneyimi anlat
units.guide:
## Yapı
Phrasal verb'ler (fiil + edat/zarf) C1 konuşmasının en doğal parçasıdır. Anlamları çoğu zaman parçalardan tahmin edilemez, dizilişleri de üç gruba ayrılır:

| Tür | Örnek | Nesne nerede? |
|---|---|---|
| Ayrılabilen | play down, bring about, turn back, put off | play **the problem** down / play down **the problem**; zamirse yalnızca **play it down** |
| Ayrılamayan | come across as, look back on, get over | come across **as** confident; get over **it** |
| Üç parçalı | live up to, own up to, come up against | live up to **our expectations** |
| Nesnesiz | turn out, fall through, bounce back | It **turned out** that… / The plan **fell through**. |

Kural: Nesne bir zamirse (*it, them, him*) ayrılabilen fiilin ortasına girer: *She played it down*, asla *She played down it*.

## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Bir radyo röportajında konuşmacının deneyimini, tutumunu ve söylemediği ama ima ettiği şeyleri anlayabilirsin.
- Hızlı konuşmada phrasal verb'leri (played it down, fell through, threw in) duyunca tanıyabilirsin.
- Kendi hayatından bir aksiliği ya da dönüm noktasını 90 saniyede, phrasal verb'lerle doğal bir şekilde anlatabilirsin.
- Röportajda zor bir soruya ya da övgüye diplomatik bir dille cevap verebilirsin.

## Strateji
- Dinlerken fiilden sonra gelen küçük kelimeye kulak ver: *turn out* ile *turn back* bambaşka anlamlar taşır.
- Phrasal verb'leri tek tek değil, cümle içinde öğren: *it didn't go down well*, *the plan fell through*.
- Anlatırken zaman sırasını kur (*We set off… By ten… In the end…*), sonra geriye dönüp değerlendir (*Looking back… In hindsight…*).
- Gölgeleme yaparken edatı yutma; vurgu çoğu zaman edata düşer: *play it DOWN*, *turn them BACK*.
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle, sonra konuşmacının duygularını anlatan ifadeleri bul.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ She played down it. ✅ She played **it down**. (Nesne zamirse ayrılabilen phrasal verb'in ortasına girer.)
- ❌ The hotel didn't live up our expectations. ✅ The hotel didn't live up **to** our expectations. (Üç parçalı fiillerde son edat atlanmaz: live up to, own up to.)

nodes.title: Zirveye yüz elli metre
nodes.description: Bir radyo röportajında dağ rehberi Priya geri dönme kararını anlatıyor

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: This is Second Thoughts, the programme about decisions people still think about. I'm Duncan Reid. My guest is Priya Nair, a mountain guide who, eight years ago, turned a group around just a hundred and fifty metres below a summit. Priya, thanks for coming in.
steps.translation: Second Thoughts'a hoş geldiniz; insanların hâlâ düşündüğü kararlarla ilgili program. Ben Duncan Reid. Konuğum Priya Nair; sekiz yıl önce bir grubu zirvenin yalnızca yüz elli metre altından geri döndüren bir dağ rehberi. Priya, geldiğiniz için teşekkürler.

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Thanks for having me. Although I should say, I'm not sure it's as dramatic as it sounds.
steps.translation: Davetiniz için teşekkürler. Ama şunu söylemeliyim, kulağa geldiği kadar dramatik olduğundan emin değilim.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: You're playing it down already.
steps.translation: Daha şimdiden küçümsüyorsunuz.

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Maybe a little. It's a habit. Guides tend to play things down; it keeps clients calm.
steps.translation: Belki biraz. Alışkanlık. Rehberler olayları küçültme eğilimindedir; müşterileri sakin tutar.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: Take us back to that morning, then.
steps.translation: O zaman bizi o sabaha götürün.

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: We set off at three a.m. There were six clients, two of them very experienced. The forecast said the wind would pick up in the afternoon, so we'd planned to be off the summit by noon.
steps.translation: Sabah üçte yola çıktık. Altı müşteri vardı, ikisi çok deneyimliydi. Tahmine göre rüzgâr öğleden sonra artacaktı, bu yüzden öğlene kadar zirveden inmiş olmayı planlamıştık.

steps.prompt: Grup sabah saat kaçta yola çıktı?

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: And how did it go?
steps.translation: Peki nasıl geçti?

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Slowly. One client was struggling with the altitude, and we lost about an hour helping him. By half past ten we were still a hundred and fifty metres below the top, and the clouds to the west had started to build up.
steps.translation: Yavaş. Bir müşteri yükseklikle zorlanıyordu ve ona yardım ederken yaklaşık bir saat kaybettik. Saat on buçukta hâlâ zirvenin yüz elli metre altındaydık ve batıdaki bulutlar yoğunlaşmaya başlamıştı.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: A hundred and fifty metres. That must have felt like nothing.
steps.translation: Yüz elli metre. Hiç gibi gelmiş olmalı.

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: That's exactly the problem. It looks like nothing. In reality, at that height, it was at least another ninety minutes up and the same down.
steps.translation: Sorun tam da bu. Hiç gibi görünüyor. Gerçekte o yükseklikte en az doksan dakika daha çıkış, bir o kadar da iniş demekti.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: So you turned them back.
steps.translation: Siz de onları geri döndürdünüz.

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: I did. And I'll be honest, it didn't go down well. Two of the clients had paid a lot of money and had been training for a year. One of them told me I'd ruined his life.
steps.translation: Evet. Dürüst olayım, hiç iyi karşılanmadı. Müşterilerden ikisi çok para ödemişti ve bir yıldır antrenman yapıyordu. Biri bana hayatını mahvettiğimi söyledi.

steps.prompt: Müşterilerden biri Priya'ya ne dedi?

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: How do you think you came across in that moment?
steps.translation: Sizce o anda nasıl bir izlenim bıraktınız?

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Probably as cold. I didn't argue. I just said, very calmly, that we were going down and that I'd explain at the hut. Arguing on a ridge is how people get hurt.
steps.translation: Muhtemelen soğuk biri gibi. Tartışmadım. Sadece çok sakin bir şekilde aşağı indiğimizi ve kulübede açıklayacağımı söyledim. Bir sırtta tartışmak insanların yaralanmasına yol açar.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: Cold, or calm?
steps.translation: Soğuk mu, sakin mi?

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: From the inside, calm. From the outside, I imagine it looked cold. Those two can be hard to tell apart.
steps.translation: İçeriden bakınca sakin. Dışarıdan bakınca soğuk göründüğünü tahmin ediyorum. Bu ikisini ayırt etmek zor olabilir.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: And did the weather prove you right?
steps.translation: Peki hava sizi haklı çıkardı mı?

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Partly. The storm came in about two hours later than forecast, which, if anything, made me look worse. Some people said we could have made it.
steps.translation: Kısmen. Fırtına tahminden yaklaşık iki saat sonra geldi, bu da beni olsa olsa daha kötü gösterdi. Bazıları başarabileceğimizi söyledi.

steps.prompt: Priya fırtınanın geç gelmesinin onu 'daha kötü gösterdiğini' söylerken ne kastediyor?
choices: Geri dönme kararı gereksizmiş gibi göründü
steps.answer: Geri dönme kararı gereksizmiş gibi göründü

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: Could you have?
steps.translation: Başarabilir miydiniz?

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Possibly. But 'possibly' isn't good enough when it's other people's lives. I'd rather explain a failed summit than a rescue.
steps.translation: Belki. Ama söz konusu başkalarının hayatı olunca 'belki' yeterli değil. Bir kurtarma operasyonunu açıklamaktansa başarısız bir zirve denemesini açıklamayı tercih ederim.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: Did anyone come round to your point of view?
steps.translation: Bakış açınıza yaklaşan oldu mu?

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Surprisingly, yes. The man who said I'd ruined his life wrote to me a month later. He'd read about another team that was caught on the same ridge that season. He didn't apologise, exactly, but he thanked me.
steps.translation: Şaşırtıcı ama evet. Hayatını mahvettiğimi söyleyen adam bir ay sonra bana yazdı. O sezon aynı sırtta fırtınaya yakalanan başka bir ekibi okumuştu. Tam olarak özür dilemedi ama bana teşekkür etti.

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: That must have meant a lot.
steps.translation: Bu sizin için çok şey ifade etmiş olmalı.

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: It did. More than I let on at the time.
steps.translation: Etti. O zaman belli ettiğimden çok daha fazla.

steps.prompt: Priya bu mektuptan nasıl söz ediyor?

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: And did the experience bring about any changes in how you work?
steps.translation: Peki bu deneyim çalışma biçiminizde değişikliğe yol açtı mı?

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: A few. We now agree a turnaround time with the group before we set off, in writing. That way, when the moment comes, it isn't my decision against theirs. It's the plan we all signed up to.
steps.translation: Birkaç tane. Artık yola çıkmadan önce grupla bir dönüş saatini yazılı olarak kararlaştırıyoruz. Böylece o an geldiğinde benim kararım onlarınkine karşı olmuyor. Hepimizin kabul ettiği plan oluyor.

steps.prompt: "It's the plan we all signed up to" cümlesindeki "It" neyi ifade ediyor?

steps.speaker: Duncan
steps.text: Priya Nair, thank you.
steps.translation: Priya Nair, teşekkürler.

steps.speaker: Priya
steps.text: Thank you, Duncan.
steps.translation: Ben teşekkür ederim, Duncan.

units.title: Güçlü eşdizimler
units.description: Doğal eşdizimlerle (heavy traffic, bitterly disappointed, raise concerns) daha güçlü ve akıcı anlat
units.guide:
## Yapı
Eşdizim (collocation), birlikte kullanılmaya alışmış kelime çiftidir. Anlamı tahmin etmek kolaydır ama hangi kelimenin seçileceği kurala değil alışkanlığa bağlıdır. Türkçeden kelime kelime çeviri çoğu zaman yanlış eşdizim üretir.

| Tür | Örnek | Türkçe |
|---|---|---|
| zarf + sıfat | bitterly disappointed, deeply moved, highly unlikely | çok hayal kırıklığına uğramış, derinden etkilenmiş, pek olası değil |
| sıfat + isim | heavy traffic, rave reviews, a mixed reception | yoğun trafik, övgü dolu eleştiriler, karışık tepkiler |
| fiil + isim | raise concerns, draw a crowd, make a decision | endişeleri dile getirmek, kalabalık toplamak, karar vermek |
| fiil + edat | pay attention to, strike a chord with | dikkat etmek, birinin içine işlemek |

"Çok" her zaman **very** değildir: **bitterly** disappointed, **deeply** moved, **highly** unlikely. "Yoğun" her zaman **crowded** değildir: **heavy** traffic.

## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Sanat ve kültür üzerine bir dergi yazısında yazarın bakışını ve eşdizimlerin bağlamdaki anlamını anlayabilirsin.
- Bir sergi açılışındaki doğal sohbeti ilk dinleyişte takip edebilirsin.
- Güçlü eşdizimlerle (deeply moved, rave reviews, sold out) duygunu ve değerlendirmeni anlatabilirsin.
- Bir sanat deneyimini anlatan, eşdizim yoğun 220–260 kelimelik bir blog yazısı yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- Kelimeyi tek başına değil, yanındaki kelimeyle öğren: "concern" yerine **raise concerns**, "traffic" yerine **heavy traffic**.
- Okurken eşdizimlerin altını çiz ve defterinde "zarf + sıfat", "fiil + isim" diye grupla.
- Yazarken **very** ve **big** yerine daha güçlü bir eşdizim ara: very sad → **bitterly disappointed**, a big crowd → **drew a huge crowd**.
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle; sonra metni açıp duyduğun eşdizimleri bul.

## Model metin
> Why I Keep Thinking About a Small Concert in Balat
>
> Last Friday I went to a concert that I almost missed. There was heavy traffic on the way, it was pouring with rain, and I was seriously tempted to turn back. I am very glad I didn't.
>
> The concert took place in an old stone house in Balat, where a string quartet played music by Turkish composers of the early twentieth century. The room was tiny, and the event had sold out within a few hours, so about forty of us sat on folding chairs, almost close enough to touch the musicians.
>
> What struck me first was the silence. In a city as busy as ours, it is rare to hear forty people holding their breath. The second piece, a slow song written for a lost brother, struck a chord with everyone. The woman next to me was quietly crying, and I have to admit that I was deeply moved too.
>
> Not everything worked, of course. The last piece fell flat, partly because the cellist seemed exhausted, and the lighting made it hard to read the programme. These are minor complaints, though.
>
> The quartet has received rave reviews this season, and it is easy to see why. They play with real feeling, but they never show off. If you get the chance to see them, I would strongly recommend it. Book early, take an umbrella, and pay close attention to the slow movements. They will make a lasting impression on you.

nodes.title: Moda'da bir sergi
nodes.description: Elif, Moda'daki kafesinde genç bir ressamın sergisini açıyor; Mia ve Deniz de orada

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Elif, I have to say, I'm pleasantly surprised. I've never seen the Moda branch this crowded on a Tuesday evening.
steps.translation: Elif, söylemeliyim ki hoş bir sürpriz bu. Moda şubesini bir salı akşamı hiç bu kadar kalabalık görmemiştim.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Neither have I! When Derya asked if she could hang her paintings here, I was frankly a bit doubtful. I thought only her friends would turn up.
steps.translation: Ben de görmemiştim! Derya resimlerini buraya asıp asamayacağını sorduğunda açıkçası biraz şüpheliydim. Sadece arkadaşlarının geleceğini düşünmüştüm.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Well, it's certainly drawn a crowd. Is that her by the window, the woman in the green coat?
steps.translation: Eh, kesinlikle kalabalık topladı. Pencerenin yanındaki, yeşil paltolu kadın o mu?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Yes, that's Derya. She's painfully shy, so don't be surprised if she gives you one-word answers. But her work speaks for itself.
steps.translation: Evet, Derya o. Son derece utangaçtır, o yüzden tek kelimelik cevaplar verirse şaşırma. Ama eserleri kendini anlatıyor.

steps.prompt: Elif, Derya hakkında ne söylüyor?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Sorry I'm late. There was heavy traffic on the coast road, and I had to park miles away. What have I missed?
steps.translation: Geç kaldığım için kusura bakmayın. Sahil yolunda trafik çok yoğundu ve arabayı kilometrelerce uzağa park etmek zorunda kaldım. Ne kaçırdım?

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Nothing yet. Elif was just telling me how doubtful she was about the whole idea.
steps.translation: Henüz bir şey kaçırmadın. Elif tam da bu fikirden ne kadar şüphelendiğini anlatıyordu.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Don't make me sound so negative! It's just that I had to move six tables and close the café an hour early. That's a big risk on a busy night.
steps.translation: Beni bu kadar olumsuz gösterme! Sadece altı masayı taşımam ve kafeyi bir saat erken kapatmam gerekti. Yoğun bir gecede bu büyük bir risk.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: And was it worth it?
steps.translation: Peki buna değdi mi?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Ask me at the end of the evening. So far we've sold more tea than on a normal Tuesday, so I'm cautiously optimistic.
steps.translation: Akşamın sonunda sor. Şimdiye kadar normal bir salıdan daha fazla çay sattık, o yüzden temkinli bir şekilde iyimserim.

steps.prompt: Elif'in akşamla ilgili şu anki tutumu nasıl?

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Deniz, come and look at this one. It's my favourite. It's the ferry from Kadıköy in the rain, but all the passengers are painted in bright yellow.
steps.translation: Deniz, gel şuna bak. En sevdiğim bu. Yağmurda Kadıköy vapuru, ama bütün yolcular parlak sarıyla boyanmış.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: That's striking. It immediately caught my eye when I came in. Why yellow, I wonder?
steps.translation: Çok çarpıcı. İçeri girdiğimde hemen dikkatimi çekti. Neden sarı, merak ediyorum.

steps.speaker: Derya
steps.text: Because on grey days the people are the only warm thing on the boat. At least, that's how it feels to me.
steps.translation: Çünkü gri günlerde vapurdaki tek sıcak şey insanlar. En azından bana öyle geliyor.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Oh, hello! You must be Derya. I'm Mia, I make a podcast about life in the city. Would you mind if I recorded a few words?
steps.translation: Ah, merhaba! Sen Derya olmalısın. Ben Mia, şehir hayatı üzerine bir podcast yapıyorum. Birkaç cümle kaydetmemin sakıncası var mı?

steps.speaker: Derya
steps.text: I'm not very good at talking. But all right, if you keep it short.
steps.translation: Konuşmakta pek iyi değilimdir. Ama tamam, kısa tutarsan.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Of course. Your paintings are getting rave reviews tonight. How does that feel?
steps.translation: Tabii. Resimlerin bu akşam övgü dolu yorumlar alıyor. Bu nasıl bir duygu?

steps.speaker: Derya
steps.text: Honestly, a bit strange. For years I painted in my kitchen and showed nobody. My family thought it was a waste of time, so I was deeply touched when Elif offered me these walls.
steps.translation: Açıkçası biraz tuhaf. Yıllarca mutfağımda resim yaptım ve kimseye göstermedim. Ailem bunun zaman kaybı olduğunu düşünüyordu, o yüzden Elif bana bu duvarları önerince çok duygulandım.

steps.prompt: Derya'nın ailesi hakkında ne anlıyoruz?
choices: Bu akşam kafede onlar da var

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: And I'm bitterly disappointed that I can't afford to buy one myself.
steps.translation: Ben de birini kendim satın alamadığım için çok hayal kırıklığına uğradım.

steps.speaker: Derya
steps.text: Then I'll give you one. You took a big risk for me, and I won't forget it.
steps.translation: O zaman sana bir tane hediye ederim. Benim için büyük bir risk aldın ve bunu unutmayacağım.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Can I ask how much the ferry painting costs? My office in Karaköy has a huge empty wall, and our clients keep telling me it looks like a hospital.
steps.translation: Vapur tablosunun fiyatını sorabilir miyim? Karaköy'deki ofisimde kocaman boş bir duvar var ve müşterilerimiz sürekli oranın hastaneye benzediğini söylüyor.

steps.speaker: Derya
steps.text: That one is already reserved, I'm afraid. A man in a grey suit asked about it first thing this evening.
steps.translation: Korkarım o çoktan ayrıldı. Gri takım elbiseli bir adam akşamın en başında onu sordu.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: That's a shame. What about the one next to it, with the fishermen on the bridge?
steps.translation: Ne yazık. Peki yanındaki, köprüdeki balıkçıların olduğu tablo?

steps.speaker: Derya
steps.text: That one is still available. But I should warn you, people either love it or hate it. My teacher said the colours were far too loud.
steps.translation: O hâlâ satılık. Ama seni uyarmalıyım, insanlar onu ya çok seviyor ya da hiç sevmiyor. Hocam renklerin fazlasıyla bağırdığını söylemişti.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Then it's perfect for our office. Loud colours will wake everyone up on Monday mornings.
steps.translation: O zaman ofisimiz için mükemmel. Canlı renkler pazartesi sabahları herkesi uyandırır.

steps.prompt: Deniz sonunda hangi tabloyla ilgileniyor?

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Derya, one last question for the podcast. What would you say to people who paint in secret, like you did?
steps.translation: Derya, podcast için son bir soru. Senin gibi gizlice resim yapan insanlara ne söylerdin?

steps.speaker: Derya
steps.text: Show your work to someone. It's terrifying, and some people won't like it. But keeping it in a drawer is worse. Nobody can be moved by a painting they never see.
steps.translation: Eserlerinizi birine gösterin. Çok korkutucu ve bazı insanlar beğenmeyecek. Ama onları çekmecede saklamak daha kötü. Kimse hiç görmediği bir resimden etkilenemez.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: That's a lovely way to end. Thank you.
steps.translation: Bitirmek için çok güzel bir söz. Teşekkürler.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Everyone, can I have your attention for a second? Derya would like to say a few words, and then the cake is on me!
steps.translation: Herkes, bir saniye dikkatinizi alabilir miyim? Derya birkaç söz söylemek istiyor, sonra pasta benden!

steps.prompt: Derya'nın, gizlice resim yapanlara asıl mesajı nedir?

nodes.title: Okuma: Fark edilmeme sanatı
nodes.description: Bir restoratörü anlatan dergi yazısı

exercises.passage:
The Art of Not Being Noticed

In a quiet workshop above a bakery in Cihangir, Nur Aksoy spends most of her days doing something she hopes nobody will ever notice. She is a painting conservator, and if she does her job well, the people who look at the restored works will never suspect that she was there at all.

"People imagine that we paint over old pictures," she says, laughing, as she leans over a nineteenth-century portrait of a merchant's wife. "In fact, it's almost the opposite. Our first rule is to do as little as possible, and to do nothing that cannot be undone."

The portrait in front of her arrived three months ago in a sorry state. Decades of cigarette smoke had turned the sky behind the woman a dark brown, and a poor earlier repair had left a thick layer of varnish across her face. Removing it is painstaking work. She cleans an area no bigger than a coin, checks it under a strong lamp, and only then moves on. On a good day she might finish an area the size of her hand.

It is the kind of work that requires a great deal of patience and a fair amount of courage. A single mistake can cause lasting damage, and there is rarely a second chance. "You have to be completely honest with yourself," she explains. "If you feel tired, or your hand is not steady, you stop. The painting has waited a hundred and fifty years. It can wait until tomorrow."

Not everyone shares her cautious approach. In recent years, a number of high-profile restorations around the world have raised serious concerns among art historians. In some cases, critics argue, faded colours were made so much brighter that the paintings now look brand new, and the original character of the work has been lost. Supporters of these bolder restorations reply that collections have a duty to show paintings as the artists intended, not as time and smoke have left them. Visitors, they point out, are often bitterly disappointed by dark, dull paintings they can barely see.

For her part, Nur has strong opinions on the matter, but she chooses her words carefully. "I understand the temptation. A bright picture draws a crowd. But we don't actually know exactly what the painter intended. When we guess, we should guess modestly." She points to a small corner of the portrait that she has deliberately left uncleaned. It is darker and slightly yellow. "That's a window into the past. Future conservators will have better tools than I do. I want to leave them something to compare with."

This attitude is shared by a growing number of younger conservators, many of whom trained abroad and came back to work in Turkey. They tend to record every step with photographs and notes, so that anyone can later see exactly what was done. In a profession where mistakes were once quietly painted over, this honesty is a welcome change.

Still, the job has its frustrations. Funding is unpredictable, and private owners sometimes expect miracles in a matter of weeks. "A man once brought me a family painting that had spent twenty years in a damp basement," she remembers. "He wanted it ready for his daughter's wedding the following Saturday. I had to tell him, very gently, that it was impossible."

Did he take the news well? She smiles. "Not at first. But he came back a month later, and we spent eight months on it. It was hanging in their living room before the couple had been married a year."

As the afternoon light fades, Nur switches off her lamp and covers the portrait with a cloth. Tomorrow she will begin on the merchant's wife's hands. Nobody will notice the difference, and that is exactly the point.

exercises.passage:
The Art of Not Being Noticed

In a quiet workshop above a bakery in Cihangir, Nur Aksoy spends most of her days doing something she hopes nobody will ever notice. She is a painting conservator, and if she does her job well, the people who look at the restored works will never suspect that she was there at all.

"People imagine that we paint over old pictures," she says, laughing, as she leans over a nineteenth-century portrait of a merchant's wife. "In fact, it's almost the opposite. Our first rule is to do as little as possible, and to do nothing that cannot be undone."

The portrait in front of her arrived three months ago in a sorry state. Decades of cigarette smoke had turned the sky behind the woman a dark brown, and a poor earlier repair had left a thick layer of varnish across her face. Removing it is painstaking work. She cleans an area no bigger than a coin, checks it under a strong lamp, and only then moves on. On a good day she might finish an area the size of her hand.

It is the kind of work that requires a great deal of patience and a fair amount of courage. A single mistake can cause lasting damage, and there is rarely a second chance. "You have to be completely honest with yourself," she explains. "If you feel tired, or your hand is not steady, you stop. The painting has waited a hundred and fifty years. It can wait until tomorrow."

Not everyone shares her cautious approach. In recent years, a number of high-profile restorations around the world have raised serious concerns among art historians. In some cases, critics argue, faded colours were made so much brighter that the paintings now look brand new, and the original character of the work has been lost. Supporters of these bolder restorations reply that collections have a duty to show paintings as the artists intended, not as time and smoke have left them. Visitors, they point out, are often bitterly disappointed by dark, dull paintings they can barely see.

For her part, Nur has strong opinions on the matter, but she chooses her words carefully. "I understand the temptation. A bright picture draws a crowd. But we don't actually know exactly what the painter intended. When we guess, we should guess modestly." She points to a small corner of the portrait that she has deliberately left uncleaned. It is darker and slightly yellow. "That's a window into the past. Future conservators will have better tools than I do. I want to leave them something to compare with."

This attitude is shared by a growing number of younger conservators, many of whom trained abroad and came back to work in Turkey. They tend to record every step with photographs and notes, so that anyone can later see exactly what was done. In a profession where mistakes were once quietly painted over, this honesty is a welcome change.

Still, the job has its frustrations. Funding is unpredictable, and private owners sometimes expect miracles in a matter of weeks. "A man once brought me a family painting that had spent twenty years in a damp basement," she remembers. "He wanted it ready for his daughter's wedding the following Saturday. I had to tell him, very gently, that it was impossible."

Did he take the news well? She smiles. "Not at first. But he came back a month later, and we spent eight months on it. It was hanging in their living room before the couple had been married a year."

As the afternoon light fades, Nur switches off her lamp and covers the portrait with a cloth. Tomorrow she will begin on the merchant's wife's hands. Nobody will notice the difference, and that is exactly the point.

exercises.model:
Why I Keep Thinking About a Small Concert in Balat

Last Friday I went to a concert that I almost missed. There was heavy traffic on the way, it was pouring with rain, and I was seriously tempted to turn back. I am very glad I didn't.

The concert took place in an old stone house in Balat, where a string quartet played music by Turkish composers of the early twentieth century. The room was tiny, and the event had sold out within a few hours, so about forty of us sat on folding chairs, almost close enough to touch the musicians.

What struck me first was the silence. In a city as busy as ours, it is rare to hear forty people holding their breath. The second piece, a slow song written for a lost brother, struck a chord with everyone. The woman next to me was quietly crying, and I have to admit that I was deeply moved too.

Not everything worked, of course. The last piece fell flat, partly because the cellist seemed exhausted, and the lighting made it hard to read the programme. These are minor complaints, though.

The quartet has received rave reviews this season, and it is easy to see why. They play with real feeling, but they never show off. If you get the chance to see them, I would strongly recommend it. Book early, take an umbrella, and pay close attention to the slow movements. They will make a lasting impression on you.

units.title: Ders notları
units.description: Konuşmadaki söylem belirteçlerini (to put it another way, the point is) yakala, bir dersi dinleyip özetle
units.guide:
## Yapı
Söylem belirteçleri (discourse markers), konuşmacının yön tabelalarıdır: bir fikri yeniden mi söylüyor, asıl noktayı mı vurguluyor, konuya mı dönüyor, yoksa özetliyor mu? Derste ve toplantıda bunları yakalayan, not almayı çok kolaylaştırır.

| İşlev | Belirteç | Türkçe |
|---|---|---|
| yeniden söyleme | to put it another way, in other words, what I'm getting at is | başka bir deyişle, demek istediğim şu |
| asıl noktayı vurgulama | the point is, the thing is | mesele şu ki |
| sınırlama, kabul | having said that, mind you, to be fair | bununla birlikte, gerçi, hakkını vermek gerekirse |
| konuya dönme, geçiş | anyway, going back to, moving on | neyse, konuya dönersek, devam edelim |
| özetleme | in a nutshell, so basically, in short | kısacası, özetle |

Bu belirteçler genellikle cümlenin başında gelir ve virgülle ayrılır: "**Having said that**, it took a long time."

## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Beş dakikalık bir derste ana fikri ve konuşmacının yön değiştirdiği yerleri yakalayabilirsin.
- Hızlı ve bağlantılı konuşmada söylem belirteçlerini tanıyıp not alabilirsin.
- Dinlediğin bir dersi söylem belirteçleriyle 90 saniyede sözlü olarak özetleyebilirsin.
- Bir dersin sonunda kibar ve uygun biçimde açıklama isteyebilirsin.

## Strateji
- Not alırken her şeyi yazma; belirteçleri işaret olarak kullan. **The point is** duyduğunda ana fikri yaz, **having said that** duyduğunda bir sınırlama gelecek.
- **To put it another way** ve **in other words** sonrası çoğu zaman aynı fikrin daha basit hâlidir; anlamadıysan ikinci söyleyişi bekle.
- Notlarını kısaltmalarla tut: → (sonuç), ≠ (karşıtlık), ? (soru).
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle ve soruları cevapla. Sonra metni açıp belirteçleri bul.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ To put it other words, it changed reading. ✅ **To put it another way** / **In other words**, it changed reading. (İki kalıbı karıştırma.)
- ❌ Shortly, the index changed the way we read. ✅ **In short**, the index changed the way we read. ("Kısacası" **in short**; "shortly" "birazdan" demektir.)
